jobs.occupation: Are you curious how your favorite ice cream is produced – and interested in developing training that can help others understand as well?
jobs.description:
Are you curious how your favorite ice cream is produced – and interested in developing training that can help others understand as well?
At Gram Equipment, we are looking for a student worker to our Gram Equipment Academy team, where we develop high-quality online training on our ice cream processing equipment – for internal as well as external use.

Your primary responsibility will be to translate our existing trainings into German learning experiences, review and update existing trainings and contribute to the development of new training.

You will have the opportunity to get in-depth knowledge about how the specific machine contributes to the production of ice cream, and turn it into training, that is understandable for machine operators from customer sites all around the world. 

This will require that you focus on:
• German translation. Your main focus will be to transform existing English training into clear, engaging and technically accurate German content.
• Project management.: You will get full responsibility for managing your own projects according to the goals, we set together, and we will have short weekly follow ups to coordinate your progress. 
• Stakeholder collaboration. You will have to coordinate and meet with colleagues from across the organization to gather knowledge and feedback that ensures that the training includes all important aspects and addresses the needs of both customers and your colleagues.
• Follow and bring new ideas to the existing process for developing training. The process stretches from gathering knowledge, through writing a script and finding visuals, to developing the training using text, pictures, videos and other interactive elements.
• Content creation. You will have to use creativity and writing skills to produce engaging and effective online training for our customers, using our authoring tool Genially. Templates and previous trainings are available for support and inspiration. 
• Quality Assurance. Ensure that the training is correct, of high quality and that the user experience is consistent. 
• Support the continuous development of Gram Equipment Academy.

Though you will have to work independently, we consider it a team effort to be able to provide training, so support and sparring are always within arm’s length. In general, our team is characterized by an optimistic atmosphere and an informal, humoristic tone.

We do not have any specific requirements for your education. However, we are working with technically complex ice cream processing equipment, so it will be an advantage if you either have some technical understanding of machines and processes – or at least a strong curiosity and willingness to learn.

You must also have an interest in and capabilities for developing the learning material and ensuring its quality. 

In addition, we do require the following:
• Personality: A self-driven team player with an optimistic and proactive work attitude and strong interpersonal communication skills – since you must be able to collaborate with colleagues from across the organization.
• Creative thinking: We appreciate input that drives change and that has the potential to improve our content, as well as the way we work.
• Language: Our company language is English. So, you must be able to communicate in English, both spoken and written, including the mediation of technical aspects. In addition, German language skills are essential, and you must be able to write clear German and handle technical terminology with precision.
• Skills: Some technical understanding of equipment, graphic capabilities and a visual eye for the detail.
• Work approach: Self-driven, proactive, flexible, structured, and quality-focused. 

We expect the average working hours to be 10 to 15 per week, preferably in the office for the purpose of collaboration, but also for the social aspect. The date of employment and your hour distribution will be adapted to your studies.

The position is located at our main office in Kolding, where you will find an informal atmosphere between good and dedicated colleagues. 

Application:
Please send your application and CV as soon as possible. Feel free to add any other relevant attachments showing your past work. If you have any questions for the position, please do not hesitate to reach out to Learning & Development Specialist, Cristian Buita on +45 20 82 02 64 or CRBU@gram-equipment.com, or Business Developer Teamlead, Line Andersen on +45 53 66 74 21 or LSAN@gram-equipment.com.

Gram Equipment A/S offers 

Gram Equipment A/S is the global leading supplier of advanced equipment and process installations for industrial ice production. With an extensive global network of subsidiaries, agents, sales- and service offices and around 600 employees worldwide, Gram Equipment has the optimal base for fulfilling our customers’ demands. 

The company is constantly striving to extend the portfolio of innovative solutions. We aim to ensure that our customers always can react fast to the demands from their customers and consumers worldwide. 

Our vision: We ensure our customers’ success in the ice cream industry by providing innovative solutions and services, while seeking to minimize the environmental impact of our solutions and footprint.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Software Engineering: Program Analysis and Repository Mining
jobs.description:
A 2-year postdoctoral researcher position is available at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) in the Software Engineering section of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI). The successful candidate will contribute to the VILLUM Experiment project “Is Correctness Necessary? An Experiment in Test-Free Program Repair.” The project investigates whether software bugs can be repaired using information found in the code itself, without relying on test suites or specifications. The position is available from February 1, 2027. 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Project Description

Generating code is becoming cheap; establishing whether it is correct is not. Large language models can now produce and modify software at remarkable speed, and practices such as “vibe coding” are widening the gap between code generation and validation. Requiring a carefully designed test suite or specification for every generated fragment is unlikely to scale. Yet most automated repair techniques depend on exactly such a correctness oracle: without a failing test or specification, they have neither a clear repair target nor a way to assess a proposed change.

This project challenges that dependency by investigating whether software bugs can be repaired using evidence already present in the code. It will combine program analysis with patterns mined from existing software to explore whether multiple, independent sources of evidence can guide repair when tests or specifications are unavailable. The approach will be studied across different programming languages and evaluated on both real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants. The broader aim is to determine when code contains enough information to support its own repair and when knowledge of the intended behavior remains essential.

 

What we offer 

We offer a dynamic and supportive research environment within an internationally recognized institute. You will join an open, collaborative team that values teamwork, professional diligence, and innovation. The Software Engineering section provides flexible work conditions and strong support for individual development, including mentorship and opportunities to expand your skills and responsibilities.

As part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, our section is involved in a variety of national and European research projects and enjoys a robust network of academic and industrial partners. This position provides an opportunity to engage with these collaborations and work on real-world challenges. We encourage and support our postdocs to publish their research in renowned journals and conferences, and to engage in knowledge exchange with colleagues and external research and industrial partners. The working language is English, and we pride ourselves on a diverse, inclusive, and inspiring workplace that fosters personal and professional growth.

 

What we expect 

The appointed researcher will investigate whether software defects can be repaired without relying on test suites or specifications. The candidate will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of a framework that combines program analysis with patterns mined from existing software. The work will involve experiments with real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants across multiple programming languages. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who meets the following qualifications and characteristics:

• 
A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Programming Languages, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field.

• 
Research experience or a strong interest in one or more of the following areas: program analysis, mining software repositories, automated software engineering, software testing, or software repair.

• 
An interest in software reliability challenges arising from AI-generated and AI-modified code.

• 
Experience with empirical evaluation, software repositories, or bug benchmarks is an advantage.

• 
Experience with one or more of C, Java, and Python is an advantage.

• 
Proficiency in written and spoken English, with good communication skills.

• 
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a research team.

• 
A strong research record or demonstrated research potential through publications or other relevant research outputs.

 

Workplace description 

The postdoc will be employed in the Software Engineering section at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), SDU. MMMI is an internationally recognized research institute within the Faculty of Engineering, known for its contributions to software engineering, robotics, and artificial intelligence. The Software Engineering section encompasses a range of research areas in software development, data analytics, and intelligent systems, and it plays a key role in several ongoing European projects.

Our workplace is truly international and collaborative. Researchers in the section come from diverse backgrounds and work closely together on cross-disciplinary projects. We benefit from state-of-the-art facilities and a strong administrative and technical support structure. The institute maintains close collaboration with other departments and centers at SDU, as well as with industry partners, providing a vibrant environment where theoretical research meets practical application. The position will be located on SDU’s Odense campus, which offers an attractive setting and a rich campus life in the city of Odense, Denmark’s hub for robotics and technology development.

 

Further information 

For further information, please contact Associate Professor Abhishek Tiwari (abti@mmmi.sdu.dk) or Assistant Professor Jyoti Prakash (jyp@mmmi.sdu.dk)

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from February 1, 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Key Account Manager
jobs.description:
KEY ACCOUNT MANAGER

Vald. BIRN A/S in Holstebro is looking for a technically qualified and commercially focused Key Account Manager for its sales of high quality cast iron solutions.

THE POSITION

In order to consolidate and expand our sales activities, we need to strengthen our sales team by recruiting a qualified Key Account Manager.

You will be given responsibility for strategically important customers, all of which are market-leading OEMs or system providers, including those in the truck sector. Your role will be to expand and enhance the sales turnover among existing customers, while at the same time cultivating new customer relationships. A significant part of the role also involves making sustained efforts to secure up-to-date framework agreements and contracts in addition to communicating customer requirements and expectations.

The sales process consists of offering to produce the customers’ cast iron components. Once the items are being produced, the sales work will involve continuously negotiating and adjusting the sales prices of the individual components, as well as negotiating and maintaining other commercial conditions. These conditions include packaging, logistics solutions, framework agreements for quality and delivery, and aftermarket terms.

Your normal working day will vary from administrative tasks at the office in Holstebro, where you will work closely with Production, the Production Engineering Department (PED), Business Controlling and other company stakeholders. You will also be responsible for planning and conducting your external customer visits, primarily in Europe where you can expect up to around 50 days’ travelling per year. You will also help with and prepare data and presentations for sales meetings and trade fair attendance, as well as continuously reporting to Sales Management.

As part of a cross-organisational partnership, you will familiarise yourself with the customers’ projects and thus become the most important link of the contact between the customer and your colleagues across the entire organisation.

When out visiting customers with a view to sales, you will always have a ‘One Stop Shop’ cast iron solution to call upon. By this, we mean that BIRN is able to cast, machine, assemble and surface-treat the products so that they can be delivered directly to the customer’s production line or application without further processing. This is both efficient and sustainable.

Are you looking to combine your technical curiosity and skills with a strategic responsibility for sales and long-term customer relationships in an international industrial group? If so, you may be the person we are looking for as a Key Account Manager.

YOUR DUTIES

You will be given a central role in the sales organisation, with your work including the following:

·       Responsibility for and the continued development of a portfolio of four to six major strategic customers in Europe, primarily in Scandinavia. You will be responsible for a turnover of at least € 25 million

·       Building up long-term relationships with the customers’ stakeholders in the fields of purchasing, development, quality and logistics

·       Technical and commercial advice during the customers’ development and project phases

·       Planning and conducting customer visits, contract and price negotiations and major framework agreements

·       Ongoing budget monitoring, forecasts and sales reports at customer level

·       Searching for, analysing and developing new customer potentials and market segments

·       Close internal collaboration with production engineering, quality, controlling and finance

·       Participation in sales and strategy activities across the organisation

The position involves some travel, primarily in Europe.

QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have the following:

·       Extensive advanced technical training/experience, ideally supplemented with commercial skills, e.g. engineer, marine engineer or equivalent. A skilled trade background, supplemented by commercial training or experience, is another option

·       Experience of technical sales, project sales or Key Account Management; alternatively, you will have been recently trained and have the right level of drive. The start date will be adapted to suit the right candidate

·       The ability to thrive in an outward-facing role with extensive customer contact, and to plan your day-to-day work independently

·       The ability to work in a structured manner on CRM, budgets, documentation and monitoring. You will need to be skilled in using digital tools, for processing both text and numbers

·       The ability to communicate without difficulty in English and, preferably, also in Danish – and, ideally, in the other Scandinavian languages

·       The technical flair and ability to get to grips with the customers’ business and applications

·       A passenger car driving licence and a valid passport with no travel restrictions

At a personal level, you will be skilled in relationships, persistent and curious, with the motivation to create value through collaboration based on trust and a high level of professionalism.

WHAT WE OFFER

You will become part of Vald. BIRN A/S, a solid and internationally represented industrial enterprise with strong values and a high degree of professionalism. In addition, you will receive:

·       A central, independent role with a high level of influence on customers, sales and commercial development

·       A strong professional environment with close collaboration across the Group

·       Thorough on-boarding and training in products, markets and the organisation

·       Good opportunities for both professional and personal development

·       Attractive terms and conditions of employment, including a pension scheme and health insurance

·       A good canteen scheme and active staff association

·       An informal work environment that focuses on well-being, responsibility and sustainability

ABOUT THE BIRN GROUP

Vald. BIRN A/S in Holstebro is the Group Headquarters of one of Northern Europe’s largest foundry Groups. We supply highly processed cast iron components to the truck industry and others, as well as industrial hydraulics and machine components. Sustainability, the circular economy and responsibility are integral parts of our DNA. The Group employs around 750 staff, of which around 480 are in Holstebro.

APPLICATIONS

If you have any questions about the position or the BIRN Group, please feel free to contact Group CSO Peter Frost Jepsen on tel. +45 3016 0160 or Group HR Manager Morten Madsen on tel. +45 3016 0115.

Please note that we are processing applications on a continuous basis and will close the position once we have found the right candidate. As mentioned above, the start date can be adjusted to suit the right candidate. Please submit your application via our recruitment system, which you will find at [insert link]. Candidates who proceed to a second interview can expect to complete a personality profile as part of the process.

We would encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, ethnicity or age, to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Area Manager – Main Component Exchanges (f/m/d); Location: Denmark , DK - Esbjerg, DK - Copenhagen, DK - Aarhus, Germany , DE - Bremen, DE - Hamburg, DE - Emden
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced leader with a strong track record in offshore wind operations, service delivery, or project execution? Do you thrive in dynamic environments where safety, customer focus, and operational excellence go hand in hand? Then we look forward to your application as Area Manager (f/m/d) for Main Component Exchanges!

Your position
In your new position as Area Manager (f/m/d) for the Main Component Exchanges, you will lead the regional delivery of our offshore MCE business across Northern & Central Europe or the UK. You will be accountable for regional performance and play a key role in ensuring the successful execution of complex offshore campaigns.

The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel regularly depending on your main place of work. The projects are typically short- and long-term service contracts for our clients in Northern and Central Europe as well as the UK.

Your tasks & responsibilities
As Area Manager (f/m/d), you will be responsible for the overall performance of your region and ensure that customer commitments are delivered safely, efficiently, and predictably. You will provide leadership across Project Management, Operational Management, and Marine Operations while maintaining strong relationships with customers and key stakeholders. The role combines strategic oversight with operational leadership and serves as the primary escalation point within the region.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to:

• Leading regional project and operational delivery performance
• Ensuring successful delivery of customer commitments regarding safety, quality, schedule, and cost
• Prioritizing resources and resolving cross-project conflicts
• Managing customer, operational, and project escalations
• Supporting strategic workload and capability planning
• Driving collaboration across Project Management, Operational Management, and Marine Operations
• Ensuring implementation of the MCE operating model across the region
• Supporting Sales & Business Development through customer, market and operational expertise

Your profile & qualifications
We are looking for an experienced and communicative Area Manager (f/m/d) who is passionate about Main Component Exchanges within Offshore Wind and wants to take ownership. You have a proactive and organised approach to your work.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management, or a related discipline
• Proven leadership experience in offshore wind, marine operations, energy services, or a comparable industry
• Strong understanding of project delivery, operations, and customer management
• Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders
• Excellent communication and decision-making skills
• A strong HSEQ mindset and commitment to safe execution
• Fluency in English, both written and spoken

Welcome to Semco Maritime
At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

We are looking for:

Blacksmiths

Key tasks:

Your job will involve shaping and joining heated metal in order to create products. You will be using a forge, hammering, and power tools. Job can include some physical work in hot and noisy environments. 

Your key responsibilities & duties will include:

• 
Forge and shape metal using tools such as hammers, anvils, and tongs

• 
Heat metal in a forge until it is malleable

• 
Design and create custom metalwork pieces

• 
Repair and maintain metal objects and equipment

• 
Cut and drill metal pieces to the required specifications

• 
Weld and solder metal parts together

• 
Operate machinery such as power hammers, hammers and punches, or power tools like drills, presses and hydraulic presses

• 
Maintain tools and equipment in good working condition

• 
Read and interpret blueprints and technical drawings

• 
Ensure safety standards are met in the workshop

Knowledge in a variety of blacksmithing techniques, including traditional and modern methods
